Short app name
Show \"WMK\" under the app icon, not \"WM Keyboard\"

This changes only the name under the icon, in your app drawer and on your home screen. Everywhere else, such as the Android app settings, the keyboard list and the app stores, the app keeps its full name. If you opened the app from its icon, this screen opens again when you change the name. Your launcher can take a few seconds to show the new name. If the icon goes from your home screen, add it again from the app drawer.
App language
The language of the menus and settings. Your typing languages are in Settings, then Languages
System default (%1$s)

On Android 13 and newer, this is the same setting as the app language in the Android app settings. When you change one, the other changes too. On Android 12 and older, only the settings app changes. The keyboard stays in the language of your phone.

WM Keyboard is free software. You can use it, change it and give it to other people. You must keep the copyright notice and the licence text with it.
Feedback
Report a bug
Open an issue on GitHub. Issues are public, easy to search and easy to track
Email the developer

An issue is the better first choice. Another person can have the same problem. Email is also good if your report is private. In both cases, send the Diagnostics text above with your report. It says which build and which device this is, and it never contains the text you typed.
WM Keyboard bug report

Dictionaries

The seed bigrams, the loanword map and the offensive word list are made by hand for this project, and they use its licence. The word lists you download keep the licences of their sources. The Open-source licences screen gives the full list.
This screen lists the components inside this build and the data the app can download. Press a row to read its full licence text. A row with no licence text in the app opens the terms of the provider.
Inside the app
Data packs you can download
The app downloads the data packs from the WM Keyboard data repository when you need them. Each pack keeps the licence of its source, whether you install it or not.
Online services
Only the tool that uses an online service contacts it, and only when you open that tool. The app contains no code from those services.
The app cannot read this licence text.
